track.legalName: Application to Set Aside Judgment of Guilt, A.R.S. § 13-905

citations: Ariz. R. Crim. P. 41, Forms 31(a) and 31(b), as amended by order R-24-0049, effective January 1, 2025
controllingAuthority.summary: Set aside the judgment of guilt. It is not sealing and not expungement. Discretionary: § 13-905(C) lists seven factors the court must consider. The record stays public with a set-aside annotation.

eligibleDispositions: conviction, after fulfilment of the conditions of probation or sentence and discharge by the court
exclusions: § 13-905(P): a dangerous offense; an offense requiring registration under § 13-3821; an offense with a finding of sexual motivation under § 13-118; a felony offense in which the victim is a minor under fifteen.

waitingPeriods.condition: Certificate of second chance on a class 4, 5, or 6 felony, § 13-905(K)
waitingPeriods.duration: At least two years since the person fulfilled the conditions of probation or sentence

waitingPeriods.condition: Certificate of second chance on a class 2 or 3 felony, § 13-905(K)

geography.venue: Statewide Arizona law; file in the court of conviction.

destination.name: The court where the person was convicted
destination.detail: One application per case number, and each count is addressed individually. The state or the victim must file any objection within 30 days after the application is filed.

components.notes: Required as a lodged proposed order in practice. The order includes a finding that the prosecutor received a copy of the application.

participantInputs.question: What is the case number, and which court convicted you?
What was the offence, its statute section, and its class?
Have you fulfilled the conditions of probation or sentence and been discharged by the court, and on what date?
Is any victim restitution still outstanding?
Do you have any open cases?
Do you also want to request a certificate of second chance?
Is there anything you would like the court to take into consideration?
Do you want to ask the court for a hearing?

supportingDocuments.name: Certificate of absolute discharge from ADOC
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Where the person was in ADOC custody.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Request the certificate of absolute discharge from ADOC.

supportingDocuments.name: Copy of the application delivered to the prosecutor
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Deliver a copy of the application to the prosecutor. The delivery method the court expects is not yet confirmed.

manualCompletionItems.why: Signature under penalty of perjury. No notarization.
Used only when an attorney or probation officer applies on the defendant's behalf.

rules.filing: File in the court where the person was convicted.
rules.notice: A victim who requested post-conviction notice is notified by the attorney for the state, including whether the person is eligible for a certificate of second chance. If the court denies, it must state its reasons in writing and on the record, § 13-905(I).
rules.service: A copy of the application goes to the prosecutor; the order includes a finding that the prosecutor received it. The delivery method the court expects is not yet confirmed. The state or the victim must file any objection within 30 days after the application is filed, § 13-905(H).

selfHelpStopConditions: A dangerous offense, registration, sexual motivation, or victim-under-fifteen question.
A serious offense question that controls firearm restoration.
A denial the person wants to challenge.
Anyone who actually wants sealing and is being routed to set-aside as a bridge without understanding the difference.

unresolvedQuestions.question: The method expected for delivering the application to the prosecutor remains to be confirmed.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Original review: "Approved with limitations." The amendment changes the operational treatment of participant-entered facts and routine hearings; the instruction not to automate the discretionary determinations is unchanged.

limitations.statement: Do not automate the discretionary narrative, dangerous-offense, sexual-motivation, victim-age, serious-offense, or firearm-restoration determinations.

provenance.sourceStatement: Do not automate the discretionary narrative, dangerous-offense, sexual-motivation, victim-age, serious-offense, or firearm-restoration determinations; confirm how the application copy is delivered to the prosecutor.

limitations.statement: The record stays public with a set-aside annotation. The conviction may still be used as a conviction where it would otherwise be admissible, alleged as an element, used as a prior, used by ADOT, and used as the basis for a lifetime injunction. No law enforcement agency has to redact anything.

provenance.sourceStatement: The record stays public with a set-aside annotation. The conviction may still be used as a conviction where it would otherwise be admissible, alleged as an element, used as a prior, pleaded and proved in a later prosecution, used by ADOT, and used as the basis for a lifetime injunction. No law enforcement agency has to redact anything.

limitations.statement: Certificate of second chance timing, § 13-905(K): mandatory on grant for a misdemeanor; for a class 4, 5, or 6 felony at two years; for a class 2 or 3 felony at five years. Section 13-905(L) allows only one certificate on a felony set-aside.

provenance.sourceStatement: Certificate of second chance timing, from § 13-905(K): mandatory on grant for a misdemeanor; for a class 4, 5, or 6 felony when at least two years have elapsed since the person fulfilled the conditions of probation or sentence; for a class 2 or 3 felony when at least five years have elapsed. Section 13-905(L) allows only one certificate on a felony set-aside.
